headline: Slack has launched Slack Code, which lets teams work with AI coding agents together in shared channels instead of in private sessions.
score_reason: Pool score kept: official launch by a major workplace-chat company, available on all plans, benefits are company claims.
importance_line: Software teams, including non-programmers, can now watch and steer AI coding agents in one shared place, though the productivity gains are Slack’s own claim.
source: Slack (company announcement), carried by Adaderana Biz English
summary: Slack, the workplace messaging service, has introduced Slack Code, which creates dedicated channels where team members can follow an AI coding agent’s plans, code changes and live previews and approve work before it ships. Teams can tag agents such as Anthropic’s Claude Code, Cognition’s Devin, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT and Vercel’s agents, and Slack says it is available on all plans and uses Slack’s existing permissions and admin controls.
notes: Read via Adaderana Biz English, which reproduces Slack’s announcement; credited to Slack as the original. Announcement date not stated in text.
